text: Why is choosing an unusual slice of 10.0.0.0/8 worth money later?
choices: Overlapping private space after a merger has no clean solution except renumbering or double NAT
Unusual ranges are harder to attack
explanation: 10/8 is enormous and free, so people use it casually — and then merge with a company that did the same and discover both built on 10.1.0.0/16. The decision costs nothing today and is the sort of judgement a plan document should record along with its reasoning.
